newsitem.title: USA: Pilots union sees progress in talks with American.
newsitem.headline: Pilots union sees progress in talks with American.

text.p: The pilots union on Saturday reported progress in resolving a dispute with American Airlines over commuter flights, but said it had not yet decided whether to endorse a new contract proposal.

James Sovich, president of the Allied Pilots Association, said the union would not make any more concessions in talks to avert a threatened strike by 9,000 pilots working for American, a unit of AMR Corp.

Sovich told reporters that the issue of who is to fly the new small jets American is to buy for its regional carrier, American Eagle, remained the most contentious issue in its agreement in principle with American.

He added that APA pilots, who fly American's big jets, had reached an tentative agreement with the Air Line Pilots Association, who fly Eagle's turboprops, on who would fly Eagle's new commuter jets, but American had not yet signed on.
APA and American reached an agreement in principle on a new contract on Wednesday, but the APA's board must endorse the pact and then send it to its members for ratification.

The union and American are working against a April 28 strike deadline, set following a Presidential Emergency Board convened to try to resolve the union's labor dispute with the nation's No. 2 airline.
